configKeys.effect: Gamerules that are set to FALSE while no player is online and back to TRUE as soon as the first player joins, listed by their /gamerule name so modded rules work too (e.g. Serene Seasons' doSeasonCycle). Applied by running `/gamerule <name> <value>` once per entry through the server command source with output suppressed; an unknown or misspelled name fails silently.
configKeys.range: no spec range; the per-entry validator is `o -> o instanceof String`, so ANY string passes - no check that the name is a real gamerule. The new-element supplier for config editors is "doDaylightCycle".

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.tick.ServerTickEvent.Post (@SubscribeEvent on the module itself, registered via NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize - and onInitialize only runs when the module is enabled in the config at startup, see notes)
notes:
SCOPE: the whole module is two files, 62 + 38 lines (wc -l), with no assets, no data files, no lang keys, no mixins, no commands, no items/blocks/entities, no DeferredRegister anywhere: src/main/java/.../modules/idle_gamerules/IdleGamerulesModule.java and .../modules/idle_gamerules/config/IdleGamerulesConfig.java, plus the standalone entrypoint src/main/java/.../standalone/idle_gamerules/IdleGamerulesStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_idle_gamerules"), 19 lines, delegates to StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot). No TODO/FIXME/XXX in any of the three, no dead code.

HOW IT WORKS (exact): on every ServerTickEvent.Post it reads server.getPlayerList().getPlayerCount() > 0 and compares it against the instance field lastPlayersOnline (a plain Boolean, null until the first tick, never persisted). With no transition it returns immediately, so the steady-state per-tick cost is one enabled check plus one player-count read. On a transition it builds server.createCommandSourceStack().withSuppressedOutput() - the javadoc at IdleGamerulesModule.java:52 calls this "perm level 4" - and runs server.getCommands().performPrefixedCommand(source, "gamerule <rule> <true|false>") once per configured rule, then logs one INFO line.

SIDE, justified: server-only logic. It touches no rendering, no keybinds, no Minecraft.getInstance(), no Dist.CLIENT, and the module appears in neither the "mixins" nor the "client" array of vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json (it has no mixins at all). It is on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS, so it also runs on the integrated server in single-player - see GOTCHA 3. Note the standalone jar itself is not side-restricted: build.gradle's renderModuleToml (build.gradle:507-530) emits only [[dependencies]] with side="BOTH" and no per-mod side, so vpa_idle_gamerules loads on a client too; it is the logic, not the packaging, that is server-side.

GOTCHA 1 (worth a warning box): gamerules live in the world save. If the server is stopped, crashes, or the module is disabled/uninstalled while the world is in the paused state, the world keeps doDaylightCycle=false / doWeatherCycle=false and nothing ever restores them - a player has to set them back by hand. There is no shutdown hook, no ServerStopping handler and no "restore on disable" path anywhere in the module.

GOTCHA 2: rule names are never validated. The defineList validator is `o -> o instanceof String`, so any string (an empty one, a typo, a rule from a mod that is not installed) passes config validation and only fails later as an unparseable command. Because the command source is withSuppressedOutput(), that failure produces no chat feedback, and the module's own log line (getLogger().info at IdleGamerulesModule.java:59-60, so it always prints, not only with debug_logging on) prints the full configured list plus the new value regardless of whether every rule actually applied. Symptom for a user: "the log says it set doSeasonCycle, but nothing happened."

GOTCHA 3 (single-player): because the handler is on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS, the integrated server ticks it too. At world load the first ticks can see playerCount == 0, so the module writes the rules to false and then back to true a moment later once the host is in - a harmless flicker in normal play, but it does mean every single-player world load touches those gamerules, and a crash inside that window leaves them false (GOTCHA 1).

ENABLE/DISABLE BEHAVIOUR (corrected - the first fact sheet had this backwards): the module does NOT override shouldInitialize(), but that is not what decides whether the handler gets registered. ModuleManager.initializeModules (core/ModuleManager.java:83-115) re-reads ModulesConfig.isModuleEnabled(module) at startup and calls module.initialize(...) only for the modules that are enabled THEN. So with enabled=false in the config at server start, onInitialize() never runs, NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) never happens, and turning the module on later in the session (config reload or /vpa module enable idle_gamerules, VanillaPlusAdditions.java:249-260, permission level 2) has no effect until a restart. The other direction does work live: the handler checks isModuleEnabled() on every tick (AbstractModule.isModuleEnabled -> ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled, runtime override beats config), so disabling mid-session stops it immediately. Re-enabling after such a mid-session disable self-corrects, because lastPlayersOnline is not updated while disabled: the first tick after re-enabling either sees a transition and re-applies, or correctly sees none. The one case it cannot fix is GOTCHA 1, being disabled while the world sits in the paused state.

FALLBACK: IdleGamerulesConfig.getGamerules() returns DEFAULT_GAMERULES when the ConfigValue is still null (config not built yet), so the module cannot NPE during early startup.

SERENE SEASONS (no code integration - deliberately NOT listed under optionalMods): the third default rule, doSeasonCycle, is a Serene Seasons gamerule, and both the module javadoc (IdleGamerulesModule.java:17) and the config comment (IdleGamerulesConfig.java:27) name "Serene Seasons" in prose. That is the whole coupling. There is no ModList.isLoaded check, no compileOnly dependency, no compat class, no dependency entry in neoforge.mods.toml and no mod id: a case-insensitive grep for "serene" over the entire repo (excluding .git/build/.gradle) hits exactly those two comment lines. Without Serene Seasons the /gamerule doSeasonCycle command simply fails, output is suppressed, nothing breaks, and doDaylightCycle/doWeatherCycle still pause. The mod id itself is not provable from this repository, which is why no optionalMods entry was invented for it - see "unresolved". The doc page should still mention Serene Seasons by name, because the config default ships that rule.

NAMING MISMATCH: the module's own displayName is "Idle Gamerule Pause" (IdleGamerulesModule.java:27, and that is what the generated config section calls it, test-server/config/vanillaplusadditions-common.toml:552) while the standalone jar is labelled "Vanilla Plus: Idle Gamerules" (build.gradle:442). Both names are in the wild; a doc page should lead with "Idle Gamerule Pause" and mention the jar name.

BUNDLE + STANDALONE WIRING: registered in the bundle at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:176 (`moduleManager.registerModule(new IdleGamerulesModule());`, import at line 26) - those two lines plus the standalone entrypoint are the only references to the module anywhere in src/. Standalone entry in build.gradle:442 with no mixins, no dataGlobs and no moduleDeps, so the jar is vpa_core + these two classes.

DOCS STATE: there is no docs/modules/idle_gamerules.md - this module has never had a doc page (a case-insensitive grep for "idle" over docs/ returns nothing). The only prose is the two-line README paragraph at README.md:153-154 ("#### 🌙 Idle Gamerule Pause" / "Pauses day / weather / season cycles while the server is empty and resumes them on the first join - the world doesn't drift while nobody is online."), added in commit 443fd4b (2026-07-27, the big README pass). That text does not contradict the code; it also does not mention Serene Seasons, the config key or GOTCHA 1.

HISTORY: exactly one commit ever touched the module directory - 1d9a41c, 2026-06-30, "feat(idle_gamerules): pause day/weather/season cycles while server is empty". Never modified since. The standalone entrypoint arrived separately with 29782a3 (2026-07-01, the beta.22 standalone-jar pilot, which already included idle_gamerules).

VERSION DISCREPANCY (CHANGELOG vs tags): CHANGELOG.md lists "Idle Gamerules Modul" at line 993, under the heading `## [1.0.0-beta.21] - 2026-06-28` (line 990). That heading cannot be where it shipped: the commit is dated 2026-06-30 and there is no v1.0.0-beta.21 tag in the repo at all (the tag sequence jumps v1.0.0-beta.19 -> v1.0.0-beta.22; beta.20, beta.21 and beta.24 were never tagged). The earliest tag containing 1d9a41c is v1.0.0-beta.22 (tag commit 29782a3, 2026-07-01), which is what sinceVersion records.

NOT PROVABLE FROM THE REPO (state as open, do not assert in the docs): (a) the Serene Seasons mod id - only the human name appears, see above; (b) the scope of a /gamerule write - the module runs the command once against the server command source, not per level, so whatever scope /gamerule has in the running game is what applies; the repo contains no evidence either way; (c) what performPrefixedCommand does with an unknown rule name - that is vanilla behaviour, not repo code. The repo only proves that the source has output suppressed and that the module neither checks the return value nor logs a failure.
oneLiner: While nobody is online, the server stops advancing day/night, weather and seasons, and starts them again the moment the first player logs in - so you don't come back to a world that drifted through three nights and a thunderstorm without you.
shortDescription: Pauses day/weather/season cycles while the server is empty, resumes on first join.
